sources.authors: Navarro-Moreno V, Zamora Á, Herrero R, Miragall M, Parola G, Saccone V, Baños RM.

findings.finding: Body dissatisfaction is less pronounced in people who exercise compared to those who do not.
findings.quote: body dissatisfaction (as one important factor of negative body image) was most pronounced in the non-exercise group compared to all exercise groups

findings.finding: Physical efficacy acts as a psychological mediator between exercise types like ballroom dance and body image.
findings.quote: Physical efficacy, as assessed with a standardized questionnaire, mediated the difference between type of exercise (using contrasts) and body image including perceptual, cognitive, and affective body image dimensions.

findings.finding: Dance and movement therapy shows potential benefits for body image and emotional regulation in eating disorder populations.
findings.quote: Evidence in ED populations was more limited but suggested potential benefits for body image, emotional regulation, alexithymia, and subjective well-being.

findings.finding: Interventions that incorporate dance and physical activity have positive effects on body image and pain intensity.
findings.quote: Interventions including physical activity (N=4) (e.g. aerobic exercise, dance, Pilates) consistently showed positive effects on BI and pain intensity.

principle: Body-oriented movement and dance interventions help improve body image, physical efficacy, and embodied awareness.
for_the_teacher: Focus on building the learner's sense of physical efficacy and capability through movement.
